title: Feasibility of a Connected Interface Implementation for Inpatient Care Handover
author: José Carlos Serufo Filho
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yewftfe
materials: Pre and post intervention evaluation timeline

steps.title: Obtain ethics approval and consent
steps.instruction: Secure institutional review board approval (IRB) from the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (register CAAE 82095517.3.0000.5149) and obtain written informed consent from each physician participating in the monitored handovers.

steps.title: Define study setting and schedule
steps.instruction: Conduct the study in a tertiary‑care university‑affiliated maternity unit (≈2 900 births/year, 31 beds) with five physicians on a 12‑hour duty shift; one physician acts as leader. Handovers occur twice daily at 07:00 and 19:00.

steps.title: Select eligible handover sessions
steps.instruction: Randomly select handover sessions for data collection, excluding any session where a physician declines voluntary participation.

steps.title: Analyze initial scenario and challenges
steps.instruction: Perform a literature review on electronic handovers, conduct exploratory visits to observe local handover practices, distribute a questionnaire (Tool 1) to clinical managers, assess legal EMR standards, and meet stakeholders (CIO, Local Quality & Safety Committee, Clinical Directory) to gather requirements.

steps.title: Specify functional and non‑functional requirements
steps.instruction: Document functional needs to replace variable, unstructured handover forms and non‑functional constraints (e.g., performance, security, persistence, data protection).

steps.title: Develop and pilot test the interface
steps.instruction: Create a pilot electronic handover module, obtain user impressions, redesign the template as needed, implement version control, manage code development, and record any justified omissions of specified requirements.

steps.title: Full implementation and training
steps.instruction: Promote, install, and train all end‑users on the finalized electronic handover interface, ensuring they can access individual clinical data and generate electronic written summaries.

steps.title: Train observers and data collectors
steps.instruction: Train and certify four observers on 14‑Apr‑2018; train all health‑professional and academic data collectors according to SOP_SESSIONS‑EN.pdf; pre‑test data‑collection tools with real clinical histories.

steps.title: Collect baseline (pre‑implementation) data
steps.instruction: Select 18 handover sessions randomly from 180 consecutive date‑times between April and June 2018; aim for ≈10 clinical reports per session (≈175 reports total). For each session: (a) administer Tool 1 questionnaire; (b) evaluate written handover reports with Tool 2 (check authenticity, traceability – patient name, hospital register number, bed location, date‑time, responsible professional, secure copy – and content: clinical history, diagnosis, alerts, critical values, adverse events, allergies, care plan per SBAR); (c) record session length with a chronometer (HH:MM:SS).

steps.title: Collect post‑implementation data
steps.instruction: Three months after full implementation, repeat the data‑collection procedure on another set of 18 randomly chosen handover sessions using the same tools and chronometer measurements.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze 349 clinical histories (175 pre, 175 post) to detect a 15 % effect size with α = 0.05, power = 0.80 (chi‑square test, 1 df). Summarize demographics with frequencies, means ± SD (or median ± IQR for non‑normal data). Compare primary categorical outcomes with association tests; compare secondary outcome (hand‑over length) with independent t‑test. Use a 5 % significance level and 95 % confidence intervals.

steps.title: Monitor and evaluate system efficiency
steps.instruction: Conduct a 3‑month follow‑up to assess the electronic handover’s efficiency, data‑quality improvement, security of demographic/health information, and any change in handover session length.

steps.title: Disseminate deidentified dataset
steps.instruction: Share the minimal deidentified dataset necessary to replicate study findings according to the dissemination policy.
